title: Callisto

description:
Episode 94 of a daily journey through the universe. ☄️
We visit Callisto, Jupiter's outer giant moon: almost as wide as Mercury, one of the most heavily cratered surfaces known, about 4 billion years old, the giant Valhalla impact basin, and why it could one day be a base for human explorers.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 95: Next stop, Europa Clipper. NASA's biggest planetary spacecraft, on its way to an ocean world.

#space #callisto #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: Meet Callisto. It is Jupiter's second biggest moon. About four thousand eight hundred kilometers wide, almost as big as Mercury.
And it's covered in craters. Crater on top of crater. One of the most cratered surfaces in the solar system.
segments.headline: Craters everywhere

segments.text: Its surface is about four billion years old. No volcanoes, no plates, nothing has wiped it clean.
The biggest scar is Valhalla, a giant bullseye of rings stretching thousands of kilometers.
segments.headline: Valhalla

segments.text: Callisto takes almost seventeen days to orbit Jupiter, and always shows it the same face.
segments.headline: A slow orbit

segments.text: It orbits far outside Jupiter's deadliest radiation belts. That's why NASA studies once imagined a human base here.
segments.headline: A future base?

segments.text: Even this frozen, battered world may hide a salty ocean deep below its surface.
segments.headline: A hidden ocean?

segments.text: Callisto, Ganymede, Europa and Io. Four worlds, four completely different faces.
segments.headline: Four different worlds

segments.text: Tomorrow, we ride with a spacecraft bigger than a basketball court, racing to the moon most likely to have life. Follow, so you don't miss episode ninety-five.
